chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Harith ibn Muhammad al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Ascension, he said to Ali (peace be upon him): O Ali, I saw in Paradise a river whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and straighter than an arrow. In it were pitchers as numerous as the stars of the sky. On its shore were domes of red ruby and white pearl. Gabriel struck its bank with his wing, and it was pure musk. Then he said: I swear by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, there are trees in Paradise that clap with glorification, making a sound that the first and the last generations have never heard anything better than. They bear fruit like pomegranates. The fruit is thrown to a man, and he splits it into ninety garments. The believers are on chairs of light, and they are the white-headed honorables. And you will be their leader on the Day of Resurrection. On each man among them are two slippers whose laces are of light, illuminating before them wherever he wishes in Paradise. While he was in that state, a woman looked down upon him from above and said: Glory be to Allah, O servant of Allah, do you not have any status with us? He will say: Who are you? She will say: I am one of those about whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'So no soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort of eyes as a reward for what they used to do.' Then he said: I swear by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, seventy thousand angels will come to him every day in Paradise and call him by his name and his father's name.
So no soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort of eyes as a reward for what they used to do.
Then he said: I swear by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, seventy thousand angels will come to him every day in Paradise and call him by his name and his father's name.
ai.seo_question: What are the unique features of Paradise and the status of Ali (a) described in the Night Ascension vision?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Fadail al-Shia* elaborates on the Prophet’s (s) vision during the Mi'raj, emphasizing Ali’s (a) role as the 'leader' (Qa'id) of the believers in Paradise, a title reflecting his spiritual authority and the concept of *Al-Ghur al-Muhajjalun* (the brightly shining ones). The narrative underscores the intimate connection between the Ahl al-Bayt and the faithful, illustrated by the daily invocation of their names by seventy thousand angels, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the intercessory and guiding status of the Imams.
